Chapter 9. Virtual Memory and I/O

9.1 Address Translation
The MMU translates a virtual address into a physical address using the page table. Each entry holds a frame number and protection bits. A page table walk costs one extra memory reference, so the MMU caches recent translations in the TLB.

9.2 TLB Performance
Let $h$ be the TLB hit ratio, $t_{mem}$ the memory access time, and $t_{walk}$ the page table walk time. The effective access time is
$$EAT = h \cdot t_{mem} + (1 - h) \cdot (t_{walk} + t_{mem})$$
With $h = 0.98$ and $t_{mem} = 100$ ns the walk cost is largely amortized away.

9.3 Page Replacement
When no free frame remains, the OS evicts a page. FIFO evicts the oldest page and can suffer Belady's anomaly. LRU evicts the least recently used page and approximates OPT. Clock, also called second chance, approximates LRU with a single reference bit per frame.

9.4 DMA and Interrupts
A DMA controller moves blocks between a device and RAM without the CPU copying each word. The device raises an IRQ when the transfer completes and the CPU then runs the ISR. Programmed I/O, in contrast, busy-waits on a status register and burns CPU cycles.
